an1.258:1.1: This must be the Sujātā who, according to legend, offered the meal to the Buddha immediately before awakening near “the town of Senā” in Uruvelā. She does not seem to be mentioned elsewhere in the early texts; there are several Sujātās, but they seem to be different people. The commentary says she was the daughter of the town landowner named “Senānī”. However, this requires the spelling _senānīnigama_ (or _senānīgāma_), whereas the spelling in the early texts is _senā-nigama_, “the town of Senā”. Buddhaghosa explains the word both ways: the “military town” (_senānigama_, due to the longstanding military garrison there), or the “town belonging to Senānī” (_senānīnigama_). Given that the latter spelling is not supported by early texts, nor is there substantive evidence that Senānī even existed, I take it as the “military town”. Her second name is spelled either _seniyadhītā_ or _senānidhītā_. I accept the former, where _seniya_ means “military” and the suffix _-dhītā_ is pleonastic (cf. _sakyaputta_ = “Sakyan”, etc.), the whole meaning “woman from the military (town)”.
